candidates.label: source

Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: opponent
candidates.comment: A person who is an opponent in an exercise action. Also called adversary, competitor, rival. Examples: "Boxing Match opponent 'Mike Tyson'", "Chess Game opponent 'Deep Blue'", "Tennis Match opponent 'Serena Williams'". Distinct from participant, which is a general participant.

candidates.label: legislationLegalForce
candidates.comment: A legal force status relation between a piece of legislation and its current state of being in force. Also called: force status, legal validity, in effect status. Examples: "New Act legislationLegalForce InForce", "Old Regulation legislationLegalForce NotInForce", "Partial Amendment legislationLegalForce PartiallyInForce".

candidates.label: antagonist

candidates.label: seriousAdverseOutcome
candidates.comment: A severe complication or side effect, such as death, disability, or life-threatening conditions, that may result from a medical device or therapy. Also called severe side effect, major complication, critical adverse event. Examples: `Chemotherapy` seriousAdverseOutcome `Severe Immunosuppression`, `Surgical Procedure` seriousAdverseOutcome `Infection`, `Medical Device Implant` seriousAdverseOutcome `Device Malfunction Leading to Injury`. Distinct from `adverseOutcome`, which is a more general adverse event.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard
candidates.comment: An accessibility hazard relation between a creative work and a characteristic that poses a physiological danger to some users. Also called accessibility risk, dangerous feature, user hazard. Examples: "A video's accessibility hazard is 'flashingLights'.", "A game's accessibility hazard is 'motionSimulation'."

candidates.label: adverseOutcome
candidates.comment: An adverse outcome relation between a medical device or therapeutic procedure and a possible complication or side effect. Also called side effect, complication, negative reaction. Examples: "A surgery's adverse outcome is 'infection'.", "A medical device's adverse outcome is 'skin irritation'." Distinct from seriousAdverseOutcome, which is specifically for life-threatening or severe complications.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: loser
candidates.comment: A losing participant relation between a win action and the person who lost. Also called: defeated participant, vanquished, runner-up. Examples: "Chess Match WinAction loser Opponent B", "Race WinAction loser Second Place Runner", "Debate WinAction loser Team B".

candidates.label: object

candidates.label: legislationCommences
candidates.comment: A legislative activation relation between a piece of legislation and another legislation that it brings into legal effect. Also called brings into force, enacts, activates law, sets into effect. Examples: Legislation A legislationCommences 'Legislation B'. The enabling act legislationCommences 'the new regulations'. This decree legislationCommences 'the policy changes'.

candidates.label: legislationApplies
candidates.comment: An informative legislative transfer relation indicating that a piece of legislation incorporates or references another legislation within a different legal context, without legal binding. Also called incorporates legislation, references law, applies provisions of, draws from legislation. Examples: A national law legislationApplies 'a European Directive'. A local ordinance legislationApplies 'state regulations'. This consolidated law legislationApplies 'the original act'. Distinct from legislationTransposes, which implies a legally binding transposition.

candidates.label: legalStatus
candidates.comment: A regulatory status relation between a dietary supplement, drug, or medical entity and its legal classification, including controlled substance schedules. Also called regulatory status, legal classification, controlled substance status, drug schedule. Examples: A drug has a legalStatus of 'PrescriptionOnly'. A dietary supplement has a legalStatus of 'OverTheCounter'. A medication has a legalStatus of 'Schedule II controlled substance'. Distinct from drugClass, which is a medical classification, not a legal one.

chosen_property.label: verifies
chosen_property.definition: To confirm or establish the accuracy of something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: hasCertification
candidates.comment: A certification relation between an entity (organization, person, place, product, or service) and its associated certification. Also called holds certification, certified by, possesses certification, has accreditation. Examples: "An organization has a certification for quality management.", "A product has a certification for organic ingredients.", "A person has a certification in project management."

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: educationRequirements
candidates.comment: An education requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the educational credentials or text describing the necessary background. Also called "required education", "educational qualifications", "academic prerequisites". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' educationRequirements 'Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science'", "Occupation 'Doctor' educationRequirements 'MD'", "Job 'Teacher' educationRequirements 'Teaching Credential'".

candidates.label: eligibleQuantity
candidates.comment: An eligible quantity relation between a demand, offer, or price specification and the quantitative value representing the ordering quantities for which it is valid. Also called "valid quantity range", "order quantity limit", "bulk discount quantity". Examples: "Offer 'Bulk Discount' eligibleQuantity 'Minimum 10 units'", "Price specification eligibleQuantity '5-100 items'", "Shipping charge eligibleQuantity 'Over 50 kg'".

candidates.label: meetsEmissionStandard
candidates.comment: An emission standard compliance relation between a vehicle and the qualitative value, text, or URL indicating the emission standard it meets. Also called: emission compliant, environmentally certified, low emission. Examples: "Electric Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Zero Emission'", "New Diesel Car meetsEmissionStandard 'Euro 6'", "Hybrid Vehicle meetsEmissionStandard 'CARB LEV III'".

candidates.label: hasCredential
candidates.comment: A credential relation between an organization or person and an awarded credential. Also called holds credential, awarded credential, possesses credential. Examples: "A person has a credential as a licensed engineer.", "An organization has a credential for business excellence.", "The professional has a credential in data science."

candidates.label: certificationIdentification
candidates.comment: An identification relation for a certification instance, providing its unique identifier. Also called "certification ID", "certificate number", "registration ID". Examples: "ISO 9001 certification certificationIdentification 'CERT-12345'", "Organic certification certificationIdentification 'BIO-XYZ'".

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

chosen_property.label: monitors
chosen_property.definition: To observe, track, or supervise something.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property fits the relation.

candidates.label: screenCount
candidates.comment: The total number of projection screens available within a movie theater. Also called number of screens, theater screens, cinema screens. Examples: `Multiplex Cinema` screenCount `12`, `Local Movie House` screenCount `3`, `IMAX Theater` screenCount `1`.

candidates.label: videoQuality
candidates.comment: A video quality relation between a video object and its level of visual fidelity. Also called video resolution, visual quality, picture quality. Examples: "VideoObject videoQuality 'HD'", "VideoObject videoQuality '4K'", "VideoObject videoQuality 'SD'".

candidates.label: displayLocation
candidates.comment: A display location relation between a creative work or product and the place where it can be viewed or experienced in-person. Also called "viewing location", "exhibition place", "experience venue". Examples: "Painting 'Mona Lisa' displayLocation 'Louvre Museum'", "Product 'New Car Model' displayLocation 'Dealership Showroom'", "Sculpture displayLocation 'Art Gallery'".

candidates.label: variableMeasured
candidates.comment: A variable measured relation between a dataset or observation and the variables that are measured within it. Also called measured variable, data variable, observation parameter. Examples: "Dataset variableMeasured 'Temperature'", "Observation variableMeasured 'Humidity'", "Dataset variableMeasured 'Patient Age'".

candidates.label: cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats
candidates.comment: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 in the ED or overflow locations awaiting an inpatient bed and on a mechanical ventilator. Also called: ED/overflow ventilated COVID patients, C19 overflow mechanical ventilation, emergency ventilated COVID patients. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 of mech vent pats "3", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 of mech vent pats "1", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 of mech vent pats "7". Distinct from cvdNumC19MechVentPats, which is for inpatient care locations.

candidates.label: colorSwatch
candidates.comment: A visual representation for a product, providing an image object or URL of its color swatch. Also called "color image", "color sample", "swatch URL". Examples: "Product 'T-shirt' colorSwatch 'https://example.com/red-swatch.jpg'", "Product 'Paint' colorSwatch ImageObject". Distinct from color, which is the textual description of the color.

candidates.label: cvdNumC19MechVentPats
candidates.comment: A patient count relation between a CDCPMD record and the number of hospitalized patients with suspected or confirmed COVID-19 who are on a mechanical ventilator. Also called: ventilated COVID patients, C19 mechanical ventilation, COVID patients on vents. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num c19 mech vent pats "15", "Facility B Report" cvd num c19 mech vent pats "5", "Medical Center C" cvd num c19 mech vent pats "30". Distinct from cvdNumC19OFMechVentPats, which is for ED/overflow locations.

candidates.label: cvdNumVent
candidates.comment: A capacity relation between a CDCPMD record and the total number of mechanical ventilators available. Also called: total ventilators, available ventilators, ventilator count. Examples: "Hospital A Data" cvd num vent "100", "Facility B Report" cvd num vent "40", "Medical Center C" cvd num vent "200". Distinct from cvdNumVentUse, which is the number of ventilators in use.

candidates.label: cargoVolume
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement of the available volume for cargo or luggage in a vehicle. Also called "trunk volume", "luggage capacity", "storage volume". Examples: "Car vehicle cargoVolume 400 LTR", "Truck vehicle cargoVolume 100 FTQ".

candidates.label: isLiveBroadcast
candidates.comment: A broadcast status relation indicating whether a broadcast event is being transmitted in real-time. Also called live stream, real-time broadcast, live transmission. Examples: A sports game broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A news report broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'true'. A recorded TV show broadcast has isLiveBroadcast set to 'false'.
